messages:
jon: FYI saw a sudden bump in 502/504 on hosted gateway after the 02:42 canary roll. p95 and p99 latency shot up, a few customer tickets incoming. anyone on call? :rotating_light:
maria: I'm on it. which route?
jon: /v1/generate, mostly short prompts. spike starts at 02:44 UTC. dashboards: https://observability.redwood/metrics/route/generate
sara: paging now, grabbing traces. oncall should have the heap of spans.
deepak: looking at canary config diff: new flag `x-tenant-optimized=false` landed in the canary config map. mainline still defaults to true. that header is used by the routing layer to pick batching kernels.
kevin-sre: that mismatch could bypass the batcher and send single-token loads to workers expecting batched KV cache usage -> KV cache churn and token timeouts. seeing `kv: miss` spam in canary logs.
maria: whose change was that? I scanned PR #4089 and saw the header introduced without canary guard.
jon: PR shows author = @maria, there was a note about testing a tenant fallback case. seems it accidentally got included in the canary manifest.
deepak: repro with curl against canary host:
```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood.com/v1/generate \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
 -H "X-Tenant-Optimized: false" \ 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-open-qa-2","input":"hi","max_tokens":64}' -i
```
Result: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout, body: {"error":"upstream timeout"}
lina-cs: customer (nova-pay) opened a ticket: intermittent timeouts, even at low request rates. they're worried about data loss. I've escalated and asked for rollback.
sara: recommend pinning canary traffic to 0% immediately and trigger rollback if errors persist.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started by @maria at 2026-03-16T02:42:12Z. Canary percentage: 15%.
maria: starting manual pause. command: `orch set-canary --release 2026-03-16-0242 --percent 0`
(20s later)
kevin-sre: canary traffic drained. 5xx rate returning toward baseline after ~70s. traces show tail latencies backend-side for requests that hit canary.
deepak: confirmed cause: header/config drift enabled a codepath that disables continuous batching; this reduces prefix reuse and overloads attention kernel initialization. root cause = config change in canary without matching runtime defaults and no rollout gate.
jon: opening emergency rollback: `orch rollback --release 2026-03-16-0242 --to stable-2026-03-12`
(rollback initiated)
sara: monitoring... gateway errors dropping, p99 back to normal in ~2 minutes.
lina-cs: notified customer: "We observed a deployment-related issue that caused timeouts for some generation requests. We've rolled back the canary and are investigating. We'll follow up with an RCA within 48 hours."
maria: short list of immediate actions: 1) revert PR and remove header from canary manifests; 2) add CI check to forbid tenant-routing header changes in canary without explicit approval; 3) add an automated pre-rollout sanity check comparing p95 in staging vs canary for the first 5 minutes.\eavy: typo: (ignore)
kevin-sre: also suggest adding alert that triggers on >50% increase in route p95 during rollouts and include config diff in the alert payload.
deepak: I'll prepare a repro script and test in staging with the header toggled to measure impact on KV miss rate and kernel init time.
jon: will create PR for rollout guard and add required-review label on any config-change PRs touching serve manifests.
sara: filing incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-sre for RCA.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-144 created and assigned to eng-runtime, eng-sre.
lina-cs: customer update sent. they'll await formal RCA.
maria: thanks everyone, let's sync in the postmortem channel tomorrow with a timeline and action owners. :white_check_mark: (reacts: :thumbsup: from kevin-sre, :heart: from lina-cs)
